protocol: D-000 turn 2 of 3, same cycle as turn 1; not a fourth turn of CONTESTED D-099; refute not confirm; PREFERENCE-LADEN scoped D-006 fleet-class successor plus RULE-GOVERNED naming of the v3 reserved G03/G04 identifiers
summary: Both turn-1 findings land, and the centerpiece repair is stronger than the one I asked for. I compiled and ran the new step-5 derivation rather than reasoning about it, because the sentence 'step 1 requested exactly that CPU type and spawn succeeded, so any other ISA is unspawnable' is my own turn-1 text and I owed it the same measurement that killed my turn-3 suggestion. It holds: with POSIX_SPAWN_START_SUSPENDED and posix_spawnattr_setarchpref_np pinned to exactly one CPU type, a thin binary of the other ISA fails at spawn with EBADARCH in both directions, so on macos-15 requesting CPU_TYPE_ARM64 forecloses Rosetta before P_TRANSLATED is ever read. sysctl.proc_cputype is gone from the protocol and named in Alternatives as measured-and-rejected. The suspension claim is gone and Alternatives rejects it by name. What I have to raise is new material introduced by turn 2. The accepted ADV-D101-T1-01 repair puts a full sha256 of P immediately before each timed launch, and the launch protocol puts a purge immediately before the cold launch, so the re-hash sits between them. I measured what that does: a file at 0% page-cache residency goes to 100% resident from the hash alone. Every macOS cold sample would therefore exec a fully warm candidate, which is cold p50/p95/p99 — three of the five operative G03 quantities, the D-006 clause-3 bounds, and the defining property of the identifier this entry writes into file 08 as 'cold-cache harness'. D-006 line 736 assigns cache-state protocol to this naming act by name, so this is not harness-authoring spillover. The detection is right; only its placement in the sequence is wrong, and the fix is cheap because stat is data-free and a post-hoc hash rejects the job just as well.

objections.location: Subject, 'Path identity (ADV-D101-T1-01)' final sentence of the re-check rule, and preflight item 2, read against 'First qualified release …' steps 1-3 and 'Second-or-later release …' steps 1-6
objections.claim: The turn-2 repair reads: 'Immediately before **each** timed launch of P, repeat that check', where 'that check' is re-`stat` P **and** re-hash `sha256(P)`. The launch protocol reads: '1. purge … 2. cold C of the **candidate** (first exec after that purge)'. A full-file hash between those two steps repopulates the unified buffer cache for exactly the file whose cold read the gate measures. The cold sample is then not cold, on both macOS classes, for both commands, on every accepted VM.
objections.why: I measured the mechanism rather than asserting it. I built a mincore-based residency probe, found a system file sitting at 0 of 1443 pages resident, ran `shasum -a 256` on it — nothing else — and re-probed: 1443 of 1443 pages resident, 0.0% to 100.0%. That is the whole of the draft's re-check. The purge in step 1 is the only thing standing between the preflight launch (which already execs P once) and the cold sample, and the re-hash undoes it for P before the exec that gets timed. The blast radius is specific and it is the expensive part of the contract. Cold p50, cold p95 and cold p99 are three of the five operative G03 quantities the paired formula names, and they are the three D-006 clause 3 actually bounds at 100/150/250 ms. The first qualified release qualifies against those absolute numerals alone with no paired comparison to lean on, so the contamination lands undiluted on the base case. The paired 10% rule degrades more quietly but still degrades: both sides of the ratio are contaminated, so the ratio survives while the quantity it is computed on stops meaning cold-cache startup, and a real cold-start regression in page-in cost becomes invisible to the gate that exists to catch it. The same reasoning applies to G04 help/version RSS, which the D101-T1-N-1 disposition permits to share the G03 launch. I want to be exact about scope, because the honest reading limits the damage and the coordinator should not over-repair: the purge still flushes the dyld shared cache, frameworks and everything else P touches, so the sample is partially cold; it is the candidate binary's own pages, the one variable this gate is named for, that are warm. Two things stop this from being harness-authoring detail routed away like the steady-baseline RSS note. First, this entry already owns cache-state protocol at this altitude — it writes the purge/cold/warm order into its own bytes. Second, D-006 says so in terms, at COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md line 736: 'The EXACT machine identifiers, OS versions and cache-state protocol are pinned by the G03/G04 harness-naming, which is itself a REVIEWED decision commit'. D-101 is that act. And the file-08 cell this entry writes describes the named identifier as 'cold-cache harness, p50/p95/p99, fleet class', so the defect is in the defining property of the thing being named. I also note the interaction with the pair rule: 'warm C of the candidate immediately; no other command or binary intervenes'. If the re-check before the warm launch is implemented by shelling out to `shasum`, another binary has intervened inside the cold/warm pair, in breach of that sentence. That is a second, smaller consequence of the same placement.
objections.repair: Keep the detection; move the byte-reading half out of the purge-to-cold window. The two halves of the check have different costs: `stat` reads inode metadata and touches no data pages, so I (st_dev, st_ino) can stay exactly where the repair puts it, immediately before each timed launch, at no cache cost. The sha256 should be taken (a) before the purge that opens each cold/warm sequence and (b) after the sequence completes, rather than between the purge and the cold exec. That loses nothing, because the contract's response to any mismatch is 'reject the job and rerun preflight' — a swap detected after the fact invalidates the same samples a swap detected beforehand would have prevented, and the job is discarded either way; the check is not gating an irreversible act. If the coordinator wants a hash inside the window regardless, the only sound form is purge-after-hash (hash, then purge, then cold exec), which contradicts the word 'immediately' and should then be written out explicitly as hash-purge-exec rather than left to the reader. Please also state that both halves are performed in-process by the harness parent, not by invoking `shasum` or another external binary, so that the check cannot itself be the 'other command or binary' the cold/warm pair rule forbids. One further sentence would close the class: say plainly that no step of the identity protocol may read P's bytes between the purge and the cold exec, so a later successor does not reintroduce this through a different clause.

objections.location: Subject, dispositions table row ADV-D101-T1-01, against preflight item 2 and the placement of the 'Path identity' paragraph
objections.claim: The disposition row states the repair without a platform qualifier — 'Path/inode/digest are checked before spawn, after observations, and immediately before each timed launch' — but the contract implements it on macOS only. Preflight item 2 says 'On macOS, re-check I and D after observations and immediately before each timed launch (item 10)', and the 'Path identity' paragraph sits inside the macOS protocol, between its header and its numbered steps. On `ubuntu-24.04` and `ubuntu-24.04-arm` no timed launch has any path, inode or digest re-check at all.
objections.why: The Linux protocol's identity binding is `/proc/T/exe` hashed through an fd at step 6, and that is genuinely stronger than the macOS path hash — but it binds the preflight child only, and step 9 SIGKILLs that child and discards the launch. Every Linux timed launch afterwards execs P from the path with nothing but D0, recorded once at preflight, standing behind it. That is precisely the exposure ADV-D101-T1-01 named on macOS, unrepaired on half the fleet, while the disposition row reads as though the whole fleet were covered. I am raising the honesty gap rather than the exposure size: the threat model here is a job mutating its own digest-addressed projection, which the contract already forbids in item 2, so the residual risk on Linux is small — but it is the same small risk the macOS repair was accepted to close, and a reader of the disposition table cannot tell that two of four classes are outside it. This is a SHOULD-FIX and not a MUST-FIX because nothing in the contract becomes false: item 2's 'On macOS' is accurate about what the contract does. It is the summary of the repair that overstates its reach. Note the two findings interact and should be repaired together, not separately: extending the rule to Linux verbatim would export D101-T2-MF-1's cold-cache contamination to `ubuntu-24.04` and `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, where `drop_caches` is the purge, so extending the current wording would make things worse rather than better.
objections.repair: Either scope the disposition row to what the contract does — 'on macOS' — and say in one sentence why Linux is treated differently, or extend the rule to Linux in the corrected form D101-T2-MF-1 asks for: `stat` immediately before each timed launch on both platforms, full re-hash before the purge and after each cold/warm sequence on both platforms. I prefer the second, because the asymmetry has no principled basis once the preflight child is dead: `/proc/T/exe` is an argument about the preflight launch, not about the timed ones, and the draft's own sentence contrasting the two bindings is about that launch. Whichever is chosen, the disposition row and preflight item 2 should agree on their face, since the row is what a later cycle reads to learn whether ADV-D101-T1-01 was closed.

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, preflight item 3 and step 5's first derivation conjunct
notesNonBlocking.observation: H is defined as 'Host arch H = `uname -m`' and the derivation's first conjunct is 'H (`uname -m`) must match the class'. `uname -m` is caller-relative, not a host fact: I ran it both ways on this Apple Silicon host and got arm64 natively and x86_64 under `arch -x86_64`, from the same universal `/usr/bin/uname`. So H is the inspecting process's reported architecture, and a translated harness parent on macos-15 would report x86_64. This is not a finding for two reasons and I want both on the record. It fails closed: on macos-15 a translated parent yields H = x86_64, which does not match the class, and the job rejects. And it is no longer load-bearing, because the conjuncts that establish T's ISA now do so without H — the spawn preference forecloses the other ISA at exec time and P_TRANSLATED discriminates translation on the target itself.
notesNonBlocking.note: Non-blocking. No repair required. Recorded because the label 'Host arch' invites a later cycle to lean on H as a property of the machine, which it is not; 'arch reported by the harness parent' would be exact. E is already correctly marked 'not the process-ABI field'.

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, step 5 parenthetical and the matching Alternatives entry for `task_for_pid`
notesNonBlocking.observation: Both say `task_for_pid` plus a target-memory Mach-O header 'needs entitlements the hosted runner will not grant'. I did not measure this and will not, because the test needs root on the user's machine and this is a review. Flagging it on the reasoning: the documented gate on `task_for_pid` is caller privilege — root, or the same euid — together with the target not being SIP-protected or hardened-runtime-signed without get-task-allow, rather than an entitlement the caller must hold; and this contract already assumes passwordless sudo, since it runs `sudo purge` in every cold sequence. The rejection may well be right for adjacent reasons: the measurement projection may end up hardened-runtime signed, and taking task ports on a shared runner is a heavier posture than this gate needs. But the stated reason is probably not the operative one.
notesNonBlocking.note: Non-blocking, and nothing in the adopted protocol depends on it.
